claim: Similar pairs yield more listed differences than dissimilar pairs, and the excess is almost all alignable differences (Exp1 11.44 vs 5.88 pairs; alignable 8.97 vs 3.88; nonalignable flat).
agent_test: Give the agent two near examples versus two far ones and count alignable differences it lists; check the extra items are structural, not surface.

claim: Alignable differences also count more in rated similarity and in choices than nonalignable ones; the 1996 triad and word-pair regressions agree, though the 1996 coefficient comparison for set sizes is small (8 stimulus sets). CONTESTED by Estes and Hasson (2004, geometric stimuli, second-hand): nonalignable differences had a larger effect; Ichien et al 2024 (N=184) attribute the similarity/difference asymmetry to cognitive complexity, not alignability.
agent_test: Force explicit alignment pairs before a judgment and compare judgments with and without.

claim: Side-by-side comparison of cases improves detection of anomalous features and transfer in humans: high-alignable accuracy 0.87 vs single 0.61 (Exp1), 0.66 vs 0.52 (Exp2); transfer 0.27 vs 0.14 (Exp3).
agent_test: Show two aligned examples versus one at equal tokens; measure transfer to novel items.

claim: Comparing two cases beats studying them separately for schema abstraction and transfer in negotiation: trade-off solutions 59% vs 22%; contingent contracts 38% vs 16%; analogical encoding 70% vs 55% (Exp3) with guided 90%.
agent_test: Ask the agent to compare two worked solutions and state the shared schema before solving a new item; compare with sequential study.

claim: Relational language (labels) helps children carry over relations: 3;8y 72% vs 45% (Exp1); 4;7y 65% vs 45%; labels that fit the relation (top-middle-bottom 62% vs on-in-under 40%) work better. Effect is age-gated.
agent_test: Give the agent a short relational label for the found structure and see if later transfer improves; only the Gentner lab reports the child data.

claim: Adult replication/extension: higher alignment and a relational label improve repair and transfer (braces 78% vs 41%; transfer 84% vs 53%; label 88% vs 50%).
agent_test: Same as label test above with adult-style engineering tasks.

claim: Joint interpretation with explicit correspondence listing improves analogical learning beyond separate interpretation; the effect is carried by the listing condition only.
agent_test: Require the agent to list correspondences explicitly, then ablate.

claim: Contrastive chain-of-thought (valid plus invalid reasoning) lifts GPT-3.5 by 9.8 pts on GSM8K (69.2 to 79.0) and 16.0 on Bamboogle; with self-consistency +15.2 on GSM8K. Checked against the paper. Ablation: every invalid-rationale type helped (GSM8K 76.0 to 80.2). R1 report says few-shot prompting degrades it, so the gain may not carry to reasoning models.
agent_test: Run contrastive demos at equal tokens versus plain CoT with a different model; check the gain survives modern models.

claim: Self-generated analogical exemplars give modest gains over fixed 5-shot CoT for strong models (GPT-3.5 GSM8K 77.8 vs 76.7; MATH 37.3 vs 34.9) and larger gains for weak/older ones; weaker models than text-davinci-002 do better with manual exemplars. Retrieved exemplars did as well or better than self-generated ones for weaker models (text-davinci-002: 47 vs 48; smaller models retrieved better); self-generated won only for text-davinci-003 (61 vs 54).
agent_test: Compare self-generated analogues with retrieved and fixed exemplars at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs are brittle on counterfactual letter-string analogies: humans 0.753 vs GPT-3 0.488, GPT-3.5 0.350, GPT-4 0.452; humans stay flat across permuted alphabets, models fall.
agent_test: Test the agent on altered-alphabet and altered-rule variants; contested by Webb et al 2024 reply.

claim: Webb, Holyoak and Lu 2024 reply finds GPT-4 alternate-rule errors 46% vs 39% in humans and no old/new alphabet difference (P=0.52), disputing the claim of no generalisation. Reply adds: GPT-4 plus code execution matched humans on shuffled-alphabet letter strings (P=0.496 vs humans, N=99/97) while plain GPT-4 did not (P=8.9e-13); failure attributed to counting.
agent_test: Rerun both sets of items on one agent with code-execution on and off.

claim: Model analogy is sensitive to answer position and surface changes: GPT-4 89% when the correct story is first vs 61% second; humans show no order effect (~.78).
agent_test: Shuffle option order and re-score; accept answers only if stable across orderings.

claim: Models handle near story analogies but fail far ones: ARN humans 97.9/94.1 near/far vs models 75.0/39.6; StoryAnalogy ChatGPT ~30% vs humans 85.7%; WHL GPT-3 far p=0.065. (Sourati figures not re-opened.) AnaloBench: given four candidates GPT-4 scores 89.1/66.5/60.7 (1/10/30 sentences) but story-bank retrieval is near random, so retrieval is the main bottleneck.
agent_test: Probe the agent with far analogy items; this is a limit on source retrieval from memory, not on same-context comparison.

claim: LLM letter-string performance drops when the alphabet changes: GPT-4o .85/.63/.48 Latin/Greek/Symbol; adults .88/.91/.89; children .62/.66/.67 (verified).
agent_test: Check transfer under symbol substitution; use as a generalisation guard.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: No source found that tests alignable vs nonalignable difference effects on LLMs directly; the gap is open.
agent_test: Build triad items with alignable vs nonalignable differences and test LLM similarity ratings.

claim: Alfieri et al meta-analysis was again not opened this run (lab URL and ERIC failed). No figure from it may be used.
agent_test: Read the meta-analysis and critique before relying on size of comparison effects.

claim: Human similarity/difference asymmetry for relational information is explained better by cognitive complexity of relations and of difference judgments than by alignability: relational trials .81 similarity vs .69 difference, featural .84 vs .84 (N=184); the effect shrinks when stories are encoded one at a time (N=129, chi2(1)=4.82, p=.03).
agent_test: Ask the agent for both what is shared and what differs; check whether relational difference detection lags relational similarity.

claim: Far-analogy failures of LLMs lie mostly in retrieval, not mapping: with four candidates GPT-4 reaches 89.1% on one-sentence stories, but finding analogous stories in a bank is near random for 10 and 30 sentences.
agent_test: Store cases with relational summaries; compare retrieve-by-surface against retrieve-by-structure, then map in context.

claim: Self-generated analogues beat retrieved exemplars only for the strongest base model tested (text-davinci-003 61 vs 54 on GSM8K); for weaker models retrieval wins, and for GPT-3.5 the gain over fixed 5-shot is +1.1 GSM8K and +2.4 MATH. Largest gain is on Codeforces (Acc@1 11 to 15, with knowledge).
agent_test: Test self-generated versus retrieved analogues per task on the target model; use self-generation for algorithmic tasks.

claim: The shuffled-alphabet letter-string dispute mostly turns on counting and tool use: GPT-3 under 0.1 accuracy on four synthetic-alphabet rules (Hodel and West), GPT-4 plain much worse than humans, GPT-4 with code execution on par with humans (P=0.496, N=99/97).
agent_test: Give the agent code or an index tool before judging it on permuted-order analogies; score valid-alternative-rule errors.

claim: Demonstration-based comparison prompts may not suit reasoning models: DeepSeek-R1's report says few-shot prompting consistently degrades performance (no numbers). No study found testing contrastive valid-plus-invalid demonstrations on a reasoning model.
agent_test: Run contrastive demonstrations versus an instruction-only compare step on a reasoning model at equal tokens.

claim: Explicit structure forcing helps LLMs: Self-Discover lifts GPT-4 BBH 75 to 81 and T4D 52 to 85 over CoT with 10-40x fewer calls than ensembling; but this is not correspondence listing and has no equal-token control.
agent_test: Test correspondence listing against matched free-form comparison at equal tokens.
